actualImplementation: The existing AppSession retains the actual namespace and one developer client using its same already-open Vault. Explicit account actions reread actual sealed App materials, lease and identity; no whole material tree or private key is retained in the MainActor owner.

One DeveloperServices value supplies the same account transport, credential storage and cancellable anisette provider. The App owner forwards actual connect/observe/refresh/finalize/logout operations. Default services remain unavailable until real GSA/provider wiring, with no stub authorization.

Renewal reuses the actual published permanent key instead of creating orphan keys. Existing pending account intent blocks another issue before local retirement. Only the existing Coordinator/journal retires unsubmitted or authenticated-cleaned candidates before new material generation; remote/uncertain transaction states block it.
Restart accepts a changed material generation only for an actually durable retired record with candidate absence rechecked. Every active record keeps the old exact generation binding.

Acknowledged publication becomes public hash/key/generation/profile-expiry facts. Account-finalization failure preserves that observation while keeping its original storage error; no refreshed material is presented as an installed App.

Erase-only logout works with unopened/expired signing materials through the existing bounded account Record owner. A failed erase remains locally signed out, and any signing-context discard also discards retained account access before another await.

The shared peer fixture remains within its original serialized Suite, forwards outer cancellation to its actual worker and contains four new App-session methods. It creates no second peer registry, cache, queue, Vault or credential service.

Only exact owned test-resource cleanup runs in an independently awaited detached cleanup task, so cancelled workers do not immediately fail Vault Task.checkCancellation before cleanup. Initialization-failure cleanup uses the same non-forwarded cancellation boundary.

Final shared fixture cleanup reopens its real namespace manifest before generation/destroy because AppSession may have published using its own actual Vault actor. The nested AppSession helper no longer reopens from a cancelled worker; there is one final fixture resource-cleanup owner.
